atoms.text: This guide configures the LogRelay service to deliver application log files to the bucket acme-app-logs in account 123456789012. LogRelay assumes an IAM role named LogRelayDeliveryRole in your account and writes one gzip-compressed file every five minutes under the prefix app/. Create the role with a trust policy that allows the LogRelay service to call sts:AssumeRole. Attach an identity-based policy to LogRelayDeliveryRole containing a single Allow statement for the action s3:PutObject on the resource arn:aws:s3:::acme-app-logs/app/*. Do not modify the bucket policy; no bucket policy statement names this role, and the grant exists only in the role's permissions. Because the role and the bucket belong to the same account, the identity-based policy alone is sufficient for the writes to succeed. In the LogRelay console, enter the role ARN and the destination s3://acme-app-logs/app/, then choose Validate. Validation writes a zero-byte object named app/.logrelay-check, and the first delivery appears within ten minutes.

This guide configures the LogRelay service to deliver application log files to the bucket acme-app-logs in account 123456789012. LogRelay assumes an IAM role named LogRelayDeliveryRole in your account and writes one gzip-compressed file every five minutes under the prefix app/. Create the role with a trust policy that allows the LogRelay service to call sts:AssumeRole. Add a statement to the bucket policy of acme-app-logs with Effect set to Allow, the Principal element set to the role ARN arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/LogRelayDeliveryRole, the action s3:PutObject, and the resource arn:aws:s3:::acme-app-logs/app/*. Do not attach any S3 permissions to the role itself; the role has no identity-based policy for this bucket, and the grant exists only in the bucket policy. Because the role and the bucket belong to the same account, a bucket policy statement naming the role ARN is sufficient for the writes to succeed. In the LogRelay console, enter the role ARN and the destination s3://acme-app-logs/app/, then choose Validate. Validation writes a zero-byte object named app/.logrelay-check, and the first delivery appears within ten minutes.

This guide covers an on-premises TraceDrop collector that uploads gateway access logs to the bucket gateway-access-logs using long-term credentials. The collector authenticates as an IAM user named tracedrop-writer and uploads one compressed file per day under the prefix edge/. Create the user without console access and generate a single access key pair for the collector configuration file. Attach an identity-based policy directly to tracedrop-writer with one Allow statement for s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::gateway-access-logs/edge/*. Leave the bucket policy unchanged; it contains no statement that references this user, so the permission comes solely from the user's attached policy. The user and the bucket are in the same account, so no additional bucket-side grant is required. Set the collector's destination to s3://gateway-access-logs/edge/ and run the test upload command provided with the agent. Confirm that an object named edge/test-upload.txt appears, then rotate the access key every 90 days.

This guide describes how to let several SyslogBridge delivery roles write network device logs into the bucket netdev-syslog-archive. Each role is named with the prefix syslogbridge- followed by a site code, such as syslogbridge-dub or syslogbridge-sin, and all roles live in account 123456789012. Every role writes batches of newline-delimited JSON files under the prefix sites/ in the same bucket. For each role, attach an identity-based policy with an Allow statement for s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::netdev-syslog-archive/sites/*. Use the same policy document for every site so that a new role needs only the policy attached and no other change. The bucket policy is not edited, and it contains no account-level or role-level statement for these writers. Run the SyslogBridge connectivity test from each site to confirm that a marker file is written under sites/. Review the policy attachments quarterly to confirm that only roles with the syslogbridge- prefix carry the permission.

This guide describes how to let several SyslogBridge delivery roles write network device logs into the bucket netdev-syslog-archive. Each role is named with the prefix syslogbridge- followed by a site code, such as syslogbridge-dub or syslogbridge-sin, and all roles live in account 123456789012. Every role writes batches of newline-delimited JSON files under the prefix sites/ in the same bucket. Add one statement to the bucket policy with the Principal element set to the account ID 123456789012, the action s3:PutObject, and the resource arn:aws:s3:::netdev-syslog-archive/sites/*. Restrict the statement with an ArnLike condition on aws:PrincipalArn matching arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/syslogbridge-*. This single statement covers every site, so a new role needs only the matching name and no other change. The roles carry no identity-based S3 policy, and the permission comes solely from the bucket policy. Run the SyslogBridge connectivity test from each site to confirm that a marker file is written under sites/. Review the bucket policy quarterly to confirm that the condition still matches only roles with the syslogbridge- prefix.

This guide sets up AuditShip to deliver audit event logs into the bucket compliance-audit-logs, with a pre-delivery check that inspects the bucket. AuditShip assumes the role AuditShipRole in account 123456789012 and writes hourly files under the prefix audit/. Before the first delivery, the service calls GetBucketLocation and ListBucket to verify that the bucket exists and that the prefix is reachable. Attach an identity-based policy to AuditShipRole with two statements. The first allows s3:GetBucketLocation and s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::compliance-audit-logs, and the second allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::compliance-audit-logs/audit/*. The bucket policy remains unchanged, so the role's own permissions are the only source of the grant. Save the delivery configuration in the AuditShip console and select Run pre-check. A passing check reports the bucket Region and the writable prefix, after which hourly delivery starts.

This guide configures ArchiveFlow to deliver database query logs to the bucket db-query-logs while requiring server-side encryption on every object. ArchiveFlow uses the IAM role ArchiveFlowWriter in account 123456789012 and writes files under the prefix queries/. The service sends the header x-amz-server-side-encryption with the value AES256 on each upload request. Attach an identity-based policy to ArchiveFlowWriter with an Allow statement for s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::db-query-logs/queries/*. Add a condition to that statement using StringEquals on s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption with the value AES256. The bucket policy is left as it is, and the conditional grant exists only in the role's policy. Enable header-based encryption in the ArchiveFlow delivery settings and start a test delivery. If the header is missing, the request is denied with a 403 response, which appears in the delivery error log.

This guide gives the LogRelay replay worker read access to files that LogRelay has already delivered to the bucket acme-app-logs. When a downstream sink is unavailable, the worker lists the delivered files and reads them again to forward them to a secondary destination. The worker runs as the IAM role LogRelayReplayRole in account 123456789012 and reads only the prefix app/. Attach an identity-based policy to the role with an Allow statement for s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-app-logs, restricted by an s3:prefix condition of app/*. Add a second statement allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-app-logs/app/*. Do not change the bucket policy, because the read permission is carried entirely by the role. The role has no write permission, so the worker cannot alter or replace the delivered files. Start a replay for one hour of logs and compare the object count in the secondary sink with the count listed under app/.

The worker runs as the IAM role LogRelayReplayRole in account 123456789012 and reads only the prefix app/. Add a second statement with the same principal allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-app-logs/app/*. Do not attach an S3 policy to the role, because the read permission is carried entirely by the bucket policy. The bucket policy grants no write action to this principal, so the worker cannot alter or replace the delivered files. This guide separates staging and production log delivery from FlowCapture into one bucket, platform-flow-logs, using two roles with distinct prefixes. The role FlowCaptureStaging writes to the prefix staging/, and the role FlowCaptureProd writes to the prefix prod/, both in account 123456789012. Each role writes network flow records as Parquet files, and neither role should write into the other's prefix. Attach an identity-based policy to FlowCaptureStaging allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::platform-flow-logs/staging/*. Attach a separate identity-based policy to FlowCaptureProd allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::platform-flow-logs/prod/*. The bucket policy is not modified, and each prefix boundary is enforced by the resource ARN in the role's own policy. Configure each FlowCapture delivery stream with its role ARN and its prefix. Test by delivering a sample batch from each stream and checking that the files appear only under the matching prefix.

This guide configures BulkShip to upload large rotated log archives to the bucket cold-log-archive using multipart uploads. BulkShip runs as the IAM user bulkship-uploader in account 123456789012 and writes archives of up to 20 GB under the prefix rotated/. A multipart upload requires permission to put parts, to list uploaded parts, and to abort an incomplete upload. Attach an identity-based policy to bulkship-uploader with an Allow statement for s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:aws:s3:::cold-log-archive/rotated/*. Leave the bucket policy as it is, since no statement in it refers to this user. The permission therefore comes only from the policy attached to the user. Set the part size to 64 MB in the BulkShip configuration and upload a 1 GB test archive. After the upload, check that the object is listed under rotated/ and that the bucket shows no incomplete multipart uploads.

BulkShip runs as the IAM user bulkship-uploader in account 123456789012 and writes archives of up to 20 GB under the prefix rotated/. A multipart upload requires permission to put parts, to list uploaded parts, and to abort an incomplete upload. Add a statement to the bucket policy with the Principal element set to arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/bulkship-uploader, allowing s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:aws:s3:::cold-log-archive/rotated/*. The user has no attached or inline identity-based policy for this bucket. The permission therefore comes only from the bucket policy statement. Set the part size to 64 MB in the BulkShip configuration and upload a 1 GB test archive. After the upload, check that the object is listed under rotated/ and that the bucket shows no incomplete multipart uploads.
